text:
marta: Heads up — CI started failing on a couple of Vitest/Jest suites after we moved the JS SDK to ESM-first. Failing on Linux CI only, local mac M1 works.

marta: Error snippet from the failing job:
```
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module: /workspace/packages/sdk/dist/index.js
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1108:13)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:935:32)
    at Function.Module._load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:776:12)
    at Module.require (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:956:19)
    at require (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:88:18)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/workspace/packages/service/tests/client.test.ts:6:1)
```

marta: Test file just `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` and then vi/jest mocks.

samir: Hmm, is CI using Node 18 with --experimental-vm-modules? Our Docker image might be using Node 16 there. That would explain the ESM vs CJS behavior. :thinking:

lucy: I saw a flake like this before. Two common causes: 1) package exports map forces ESM and tests still use CommonJS runner; 2) transform/config not inlining the ESM packages for the test runner.

ryan: On Vitest you can force dependency inlining to avoid the ESM/CJS boundary: in vitest.config.ts -> defineConfig({ deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] } }) — that usually fixes import errors for deps distributed as ESM.

marta: We're using both Jest (legacy suites) and Vitest (new ones). Jest config currently uses ts-jest and transform ignore patterns that skip node_modules. The SDK is in our monorepo so it's resolving to dist/ which is ESM. :facepalm:

samir: For Jest you can either set "transform": {"^.+\.tsx?$": "ts-jest"} and add "extensionsToTreatAsEsm": [".ts"], or use babel-jest with an ESM-aware config. Another option is to publish a CJS-compatible entrypoint (exports map) for test env.

lucy: Also check package.json "type": "module" in the SDK package. If it's set, Node assumes ESM. For Jest we had to set package.exports to include a cjs entry: {"import": "dist/index.mjs", "require": "dist/index.cjs"}. That kept runtime and tests happy.

marta: We don't have a CJS build currently — we removed rollup CJS output to simplify pipeline. Is publishing a small CJS shim acceptable?

ryan: Short-term shim is fine. Long-term we should standardize test runners to handle ESM. For Jest on CI we also had to set NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules in the job. Vitest runs fine under native ESM since it's Vite-based.

eng-ci-bot: CI job "unit-tests:linux" failed 3 times in last 24h. Suggested labels: flaky, sdk-interop.

samir: Another wrinkle is mocking APIs — jest.mock vs vi.mock differences. In ESM-land, auto-mocking can behave differently because imports are static. If tests rely on require-time replacement, they break. Recommended pattern: prefer dependency injection or mock at module boundary with vi.mock('./http', async () => ({ default: vi.fn() })) for Vitest. For Jest with ESM you may need to use jest.unstable_mockModule (node jest native ESM helpers).

marta: Example of a flaky test that fails only on CI (Vitest):
```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'
vi.mock('@redwood/sdk', () => ({ createClient: () => ({ request: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ ok: true }) }) }))

test('calls sdk', async () => {
  const client = createClient()
  await expect(client.request('/ping')).resolves.toMatchObject({ ok: true })
})
```

marta: That code passes locally but CI sometimes resolves to the real implementation because the package was hoisted and resolved to dist with top-level await side-effects.

lucy: Side-effects at top-level in dist can cause test ordering issues. We should remove side-effects or ensure the mock path is inlined before module evaluation. Vitest has `testTimeout` and `setupFiles` ordering quirks.

ryan: Quick triage plan:
1) Pin CI Node to 18 and enable experimental flags if needed.
2) Add vitest.config.ts deps.inline for @redwood/sdk.
3) For Jest, either add a small CJS shim in package.exports or adjust transforms + extensionsToTreatAsEsm.
4) Audit SDK build for top-level side-effects and lazy-init instead.

samir: I'll open a draft PR that: adds deps.inline to the Vitest config, updates the Jest job to NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules, and adds a temporary cjs shim export. Will also add a one-off CI matrix job to reproduce locally.

marta: Awesome — please tag me. Also we should add a note in the SDK changelog: "ESM-only build may require test runner config changes" so integrators aren't surprised.

lucy: After the PR lands, let's run the monorepo test matrix (linux/macos/windows) in GH actions to ensure no platform-specific surprises.

ryan: One final typing note: TS types import require "types": "dist/index.d.ts" — if we add a cjs shim make sure types still point to the unified declaration file, otherwise consumers in Jest might pick the wrong entry.

marta: Thanks all — assigning to @samir to carry the PR. I'll monitor CI. :thumbsup:
